coordinate_definitions.axes: World Cartesian +x and +y match the native observation/action schema; +z=(0,0,1) points upward along the declared fixed peg axis. Horizontal plane is world xy. No unverified camera-to-world inference is used.
coordinate_definitions.symbols: For each raw observation, h=raw[0:3] hand, aperture=raw[3], p=raw[4:7] nut handle site, q=raw[7:11] native body wxyz quaternion, h_previous=raw[18:21], p_previous=raw[22:25], g=raw[36:39] declared goal, r=raw[39:42] observed ring center; rho=norm((r-g)[0:2]).
coordinate_definitions.units: Positions and lengths are metres, control interval 0.0125 s, velocity metres/second. Native spatial action units multiply by 0.01 m; gripper action [-1,1] is native unitless. Aperture is the declared native aperture divided by 0.1 m and is not the gripper action.
coordinate_definitions.quaternion: For each present body quaternion, normalize its Euclidean norm; use identity (1,0,0,0) if norm<1e-8. Choose sign so the first nonzero component in w,x,y,z order is positive; this represents the same rotation and never supplies extra orientation information.
coordinate_definitions.static_geometry: Only supplied material is used: vertical peg axis, peg radius 0.020 m and halfheight 0.050 m. Goal z is the declared observation target; the design does not infer a hidden success band or derive an analytic action controller from geometry.

shared_training_protocol.batch: 128 total chunks per update across the entire candidate. Sample an episode uniformly from current D_N, then a valid action start uniformly from 0..T-1 within that episode, with replacement.
shared_training_protocol.observations: Exactly two whole consecutive common raw observations; repeat initial observation for absent outer history. Retain native internal previous channels as provided; no new sensor history.
shared_training_protocol.prediction_execution: Prediction horizon 16 native actions, execute 4, replan. Training action starts at the current observation index.
shared_training_protocol.tail_handling: Repeat the final valid action only to fill the tensor to length 16; a boolean validity mask excludes every padded target from loss. Do not cross episode boundaries. Auxiliary future targets use their separate stated eligibility masks.
shared_training_protocol.optimizer: AdamW learning_rate 1e-4, weight_decay 1e-6, betas [0.9,0.999]; global gradient norm clip 1 across all modules; exactly 20,000 joint updates, batch 128 total. Maintain EMA decay 0.995 for all trainable modules and use EMA at inference.
shared_training_protocol.diffusion: Epsilon target with k uniform over integers 0..99. Cosine schedule uses f(u)=cos(((u+0.008)/1.008)*pi/2)^2 and beta_i=min(1-f((i+1)/100)/f(i/100),0.999), i=0..99. Forward corruption uses cumulative product alpha_bar. DDIM uses 16 indices round(linspace(99,0,16)), eta=0, and final clean reconstruction after index 0. No clean-sample clipping or guidance.
shared_training_protocol.action_execution: Decode the entire chunk in its fixed replan frame, then clip each native world xyz and gripper component to [-1,1] before env.step. No analytic correction, rescue, runtime action search or future state input.
shared_training_protocol.run_scope: Train N in [2,5,10,20] independently from scratch at seed 0 using only nested D_N. One formal training process on GPU 1 selected by Pixi activation. This design does not launch any run.
shared_training_protocol.design_freeze: This version precedes implementation. Any substantive feasibility revision must create a new version with reason, at most once. Later permitted N5 development feedback revision is a separately recorded process and must not rewrite this original design.

evidence_observations.interpretation: These are descriptive measurements from the two supplied successful demonstrations. They are neither a native success rule nor a new evaluation. The rendered frames show handle grasp and ring placement but do not establish robustness, recovery or visual-policy generalization.

seriously_considered: P1 explicit point relations plus P2 moving action basis.
P1 explicit point relations plus learned soft event conditioning and future-geometry supervision.
combination_consideration.adopted: P3 adopts the second combination. It preserves world actions while asking small jointly trained heads to organize relational conditioning. The shared model and predicted-only soft conditioning avoid independent controllers or teacher-forced routing.
combination_consideration.rejected_for_initial_version: Do not combine the moving action basis with the event/auxiliary candidate. D2 provides little evidence about near-alignment basis switches or recovery; coupling that discontinuity with learned sequencing would make failures harder to interpret. P2 remains the separate action-representation test.
combination_consideration.comparability_limit: P1/P2/P3 are three prospective candidate designs, not a perfectly factorial ablation. P2 adds frame-aware absolute anchors; P3 adds auxiliary capacity and losses. No winning candidate or positive result is claimed.

knowledge_hypotheses.claim: Grasp contact and insertion alignment refer to different physical points: a handle grasp does not imply that the ring center is aligned with the peg. Coordinate differences directly represent these relations.

The handle site lies approximately 0.130 m from the observed ring center throughout both trajectories; initial handle-minus-ring is approximately (+0.130,0,0) m. Both successful demonstrations lift before transporting and descending.

knowledge_hypotheses.claim: Exposing hand-to-handle and ring-to-goal relations separately may reduce reliance on the LL/HH correlation between initial nut x and peg x. D2 cannot establish extrapolation or recovery.

action_transform.normalization: No fitted action normalization; no clipping of noised or denoised clean samples inside the sampler.
action_transform.frame: World +x,+y and +z, with +z the vertical peg/gravity-opposing axis; fixed throughout every chunk.

candidates.applicability: Assembly with a fixed world vertical axis and a measurable ring-to-goal horizontal displacement. This is a coordinate representation, not a claim of physical translation or rotation symmetry.
failure_conditions: The basis switches to world x near alignment; that discontinuity can make nearby training windows have different encoded actions.
Direction inferred from a small ring-to-goal vector is noisy; the specified radius fallback limits but does not eliminate this issue.

observation_transform.basis: At replan t use r_t and g_t from s_t. Let d=(g_x-r_x,g_y-r_y,0), rho=norm(d), e_z=(0,0,1). If rho >= 0.020 m, e_1=d/rho; otherwise e_1=(1,0,0). Let e_2=e_z cross e_1 and B_t=[e_1,e_2,e_z] with columns in world coordinates. The 0.020 m cutoff equals the declared peg radius but is only a numerical coordinate rule, not an insertion or success rule.
observation_transform.history_frame: Use exactly this current B_t and current origin r_t for BOTH outer-history raw entries and every vector in the predicted chunk; do not build a different frame for the previous observation or future targets.
observation_transform.per_raw_output: Start with the same 48 slots as P1. Replace each retained position x by B_t^T(x-r_t)/0.10 m. Rotate each relation vector with B_t^T and divide by 0.10 m; rotate velocities with B_t^T and divide by 1 m/s. Keep rho, vertical gap, apertures and the canonical native WORLD wxyz quaternions as in P1. Append world h_j/0.10 m, world g_j/0.10 m, world r_j/0.10 m, and (e_1x,e_1y). This is 59 features per raw and 118 for the two entries.
observation_transform.orientation_note: Quaternions remain explicitly world-referenced; they are not asserted to be local-frame quaternions. Absolute anchors and basis components make the representation aware of fixed world geometry.
observation_transform.statistics: No learned normalization, feature clipping or augmented states. No new runtime channel.

action_transform.encode: For every action in a training chunk anchored at t, u_xyz=B_t^T a_xyz and u_g=a_g. a_xyz is native dimensionless displacement; equivalently rotate 0.01*a_xyz metres then divide by 0.01 m. Encoded spatial components may exceed magnitude 1 and must not be clipped.
action_transform.decode: For all 16 denoised actions use the same anchor B_t: a_xyz=B_t u_xyz, a_g=u_g. Clip the four resulting native WORLD components to [-1,1] only before executing them.
action_transform.normalization: Identity after basis change. No fitted action scale, clean-sample clipping or per-axis local clipping.
action_transform.runtime_replanning: Discard the unexecuted 12 predictions after four actions, build a new B from the next current observation, and replan. Never reinterpret cached encoded actions using a new basis.

knowledge_hypotheses.claim: The observed sequences support approach, grasp/lift, carry and alignment/descent as useful retrospective groups. The fixed three-observation milestone rules below give event starts [22,45,73] in demo 1 and [25,48,78] in demo 2; these labels are new design heuristics, not native simulator phases.
knowledge_hypotheses.reference: demo_1_trajectory.npz and demo_2_trajectory.npz, declared aperture, ring center and goal channels; all 16 rendered frames.

knowledge_hypotheses.claim: Carrying an object to a vertical peg couples horizontal center alignment to vertical clearance, while hand-to-handle geometry concerns grasp maintenance. Supervising both relations can separate their roles without prescribing an analytic controller.

Jointly learning event probabilities and short-horizon future relations may organize diffusion conditioning more efficiently than an unconstrained relation expansion, especially when initial object and goal x values are recombined. Successful-only labels may instead reinforce brittle sequencing.

candidates.predicted_generalization_gain: Prospectively may improve ordering and retention of grasp geometry across independent object/goal layouts. The combination may be worse at N2 because auxiliary targets and retrospective modes add bias and have no failure examples.

failure_conditions: Heuristic thresholds can partition states poorly or miss a milestone in a legitimate successful trajectory.
The four labeled modes may not describe recovery behavior, alternative grasps or off-trajectory states.
A future-relation head fit to demonstrations may encode their motion habits rather than task-invariant structure.
Diffusion and auxiliary gradients may conflict; the weights are frozen here and cannot be tuned using unseen demonstrations or initial-model scores.

architecture.conditioning_encoder: Use P1 96D features. E is Linear(96,128), SiLU, Linear(128,128), SiLU.
architecture.event_head: From E, Linear(128,64), SiLU, Linear(64,4), softmax.
architecture.future_relation_head: From E, Linear(128,64), SiLU, Linear(64,12), unconstrained output. This head is used for training and optional diagnostics, never to produce or correct actions.

Use predicted probabilities during both training and inference; no ground-truth mode is fed to the action model. Diffusion gradients pass through E and the softmax event head.
architecture.parameter_sharing: One diffusion U-Net for all modes. No per-mode expert networks or sequential training stages. One optimizer jointly updates encoder, both heads and U-Net.

modules: Four-class retrospective-event head with soft runtime conditioning.

losses_and_weights.name: event_cross_entropy
losses_and_weights.target: Four-class milestone label y_t defined in required_train_labels.
losses_and_weights.scale: Mean unweighted cross entropy over the 128 current-window labels, natural logarithms. No class reweighting.
losses_and_weights.application_condition: Every update, every sampled chunk. All milestone labels are generated only from its current D_N demonstration.

losses_and_weights.name: future_relation_smooth_l1
losses_and_weights.target: At H in {4,16} actions ahead, concatenate (r_(t+H)-g_(t+H))/0.10 m and (p_(t+H)-h_(t+H))/0.10 m: six components per horizon, twelve outputs in H=4 then H=16 order.
losses_and_weights.scale: SmoothL1 beta=1 on normalized components; mean over all valid horizon/components in the batch. H corresponds to 0.050 or 0.200 s. No fitted label normalization.
losses_and_weights.application_condition: Only horizons satisfying t+H <= T, where T is the final observation index. Invalid horizons are masked, not clamped to the terminal state. If none are valid, this term is exactly zero.

hierarchy_selection_and_termination.selection: At each replan compute the four soft event probabilities from the two common observations. Supply the entire vector to the shared diffusion model. There is no hard expert selection, argmax controller, threshold-triggered action, or forced monotonic mode sequence.
hierarchy_selection_and_termination.mode_termination: A mode relinquishes conditioning weight only through the next predicted probability vector. There is no additional learned or analytic termination module; environment episode termination is unchanged.
hierarchy_selection_and_termination.training_inference_match: Use predicted probabilities from the beginning of training, never teacher-forced class labels. Auxiliary labels supervise the event head only.
hierarchy_selection_and_termination.runtime_information: Neither retrospective milestone indices nor future relation targets are accessible at runtime. No episode clock or oracle phase is supplied.

candidates.chunk_transition_handling: Freeze E and event probabilities at replan t for the complete 16-action prediction and first four executed actions. Recompute only at the next replan; discard stale predictions. Do not relabel action targets or restart the episode clock when a labeled training boundary lies within a chunk. Every action target remains its actual demonstrated world command.

required_train_labels.actions: Current D_N native demonstration action chunks.
required_train_labels.milestone_definition: For each training episode with observations 0..T, define event(mask,start) as the smallest i >= start with i+2 <= T and mask true at all of i,i+1,i+2; if none exists return sentinel T+1. c=event(aperture<=0.85,0). l=event(r_z>=g_z+0.050 m,c). a=event(rho<=0.020 m AND r_z>=g_z+0.030 m,l). If start>T, return T+1. These fixed constants are declared design choices, not fitted success thresholds.
required_train_labels.class_rule: For every current action index t=0..T-1, y_t=1[t>=c]+1[t>=l]+1[t>=a], yielding 0 approach, 1 grasp/lift, 2 carry, 3 alignment/descent. Empty modes are permitted; do not fabricate missing events or inspect extra trajectories to revise thresholds. Three-observation persistence is retrospective training supervision only.
required_train_labels.future_relations: Use exactly the common observation channels at t+4 and t+16 with the eligibility masks specified in losses_and_weights. No simulator reward, success labels, hidden contact state or expert implementation is read.
required_train_labels.D2_rule_check: The rules produce c/l/a=22/45/73 for the 87-action LL episode and 25/48/78 for the 92-action HH episode. This checks only that the declared labels are populated in the allowed evidence; it is not a performance result.

required_runtime_inputs: The two most recent common raw observations (42 numbers each, initial repeated).
Fixed declared action scale 0.01 m, control dt 0.0125 s, and world axes.
The candidate checkpoint and normal diffusion sampling RNG. No images, future states/actions, hidden phase, success signal, source expert, or privileged physics channel.

parameter_budget.hard_cap: At most 3 times measured raw-input B0 trainable parameters, including shared encoder, router/event head, future head and conditioning layers.
parameter_budget.prospective_estimate: One default U-Net plus small MLPs; expected below 5.5 million parameters. This is an estimate, not a measured artifact. No separately trained experts.
parameter_budget.enforcement: Measure all trainable modules before training; if over cap, record an implementation feasibility issue before any substantive revision.

implementation_steps: Reuse the exact P1 world-relation and action codecs.
Implement deterministic per-episode milestone labels and future-relation labels, loading only the current D_N for each run.
Implement the shared encoder, four-way soft head and 12D auxiliary head; condition the single U-Net on predicted E/probabilities in both train and runtime paths.
Implement exact masked losses and 2,000-update ramps within one optimizer step per shared batch.
Validate synthetic end-of-episode masks, missing milestones and mode-boundary chunks; verify the D2 rule starts reported above without any new task rollouts.
Measure full parameter count, record the frozen design/configuration linkage, and train each prescribed N from scratch.

confidence.basis: The event ordering and point relations are observed; the auxiliary combination and its effect on generalization are untested.
